messages:
sara_support: Hey team, ACME SRE reported that our rerank endpoint is returning weird scores (lots of zeros and ties) after they upgraded to the new Python SDK 0.9.2. Customer says ordering is completely different from expected and some scores are strings in the UI. They filed a support ticket and attached a small repro.

acme_sre_jdoe: @sara_support yes — we saw this after bumping from 0.9.1 -> 0.9.2. Example: we send 5 candidates, get back 5 scores but three are "0.0" (strings) and two are floats like 0.742. When client displays the results it sorts lexicographically so ordering becomes wrong. Repro steps: call /v1/rerank with body we used (pasted below).

acme_sre_jdoe: Payload we POSTed:
```json
{
  "query": "best monitor for remote office",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "Dell 27"},
    {"id": "c2", "text": "LG ultrawide"},
    {"id": "c3", "text": "Asus 24"},
    {"id": "c4", "text": "Samsung 32"},
    {"id": "c5", "text": "BenQ 27"}
  ]
}
```

acme_sre_jdoe: Response snippet we got:
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"id": "c1", "score": "0.0"},
    {"id": "c2", "score": 0.742},
    {"id": "c3", "score": "0.0"},
    {"id": "c4", "score": "0.0"},
    {"id": "c5", "score": 0.681}
  ]
}
```

jon_eng: Thanks for the repro. Two quick asks: 1) which SDK method did you call (client.rerank vs client.batch_rerank)? 2) can you share the exact pip package version output (`pip show redwood-sdk`)?

acme_sre_jdoe: We used the single call `client.rerank(query, candidates)`. pip shows `redwood-sdk 0.9.2`. Also we noticed this happens intermittently — sometimes all scores are floats.

maria_ml: Looks like a serialization/parsing mismatch. We recently changed the server to emit high-precision scores and relied on SDK to parse numbers consistently. If some clients treat numbers as strings it could be a JSON encoder difference or a TypeScript/TS client bug. @alex_sdk can you investigate the Python SDK behavior around JSON loads/dumps for rerank?

alex_sdk: On it. First thing I checked: our Python SDK had a subtle change in 0.9.2 where we post-process candidate objects to preserve `id` ordering, and in some cases we `json.dumps` with default=str for unknowns. That can coerce float-like Decimals to strings. Trying to reproduce locally.

alex_sdk: Quick local repro: when candidates contain Decimal objects from user code or from upstream libs, our serializer did `str()` on those values. Example:
```py
from decimal import Decimal
import json
payload = {"results": [{"id": "c1", "score": Decimal('0.0')} ]}
json.dumps(payload, default=str)  # -> score becomes "0.0"
```
That matches the string scores. But the server should also return numbers as numbers — why only on some calls?

jon_eng: Another angle: frontend parsing showing lexicographic sort suggests client-side TS may be parsing scores as strings. Is the TS SDK converting numbers to strings when normalizing responses? @alex_sdk any similar change there?

alex_sdk: I checked the TypeScript SDK change log — we introduced a small normalization in 0.14.0 that maps result.score = String(score) to unify formatting, but that was only in the browser bundle. Seems unrelated to Python.

maria_ml: There's also a server-side bug patch we rolled last week: when request has `candidates` as an object (dict) rather than an array, the reranker internally maps keys and sometimes emits scores keyed by candidate id as strings. Could the Python SDK be sending candidates incorrectly in batched/edge cases?

acme_sre_jdoe: Hmm we double-checked our code — we pass a list. But we also use a helper that constructs candidates from a pandas DataFrame and it might be yielding a dict-like row. I can try to force `list(df.to_dict(orient=records))` and test.

sara_support: For now, workaround for ACME: can you try calling the HTTP API directly with curl (bypassing SDK) and confirm whether response uses numeric scores? If yes, the SDK is likely the root cause. Provide logs if you can.

acme_sre_jdoe: I did quick curl test and got numeric floats consistently. So it's looking like the SDK path is the issue. Example curl response:
```json
{
  "results": [{"id":"c2","score":0.742},{"id":"c5","score":0.681},{"id":"c1","score":0.01}]
}
```

alex_sdk: Thanks — that nails it. Reproduced in a unit test: when candidate.score or other fields are Decimal or numpy types, our serializer used `default=str` and converted numeric fields to strings. Also noticed Python SDK response wrapper inadvertently casts numbers to str when creating a pandas-friendly DataFrame view. I'll push a patch to stop using `default=str` and instead convert Decimals to float explicitly, plus avoid coercing response.score values to strings.

alex_sdk: Patch: change in serialize.py -> replace `json.dumps(obj, default=str)` with a small helper:
```py
def _num_safe(v):
    if isinstance(v, Decimal):
        return float(v)
    raise TypeError
json.dumps(obj, default=_num_safe)
```
I'll cut a 0.9.3 release in the next hour.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging redwood-sdk 0.9.3 -> success (artifact built, tests passed). :rocket:

alex_sdk: 0.9.3 published. Fixes: do not coerce numeric types to strings on serialization; preserve candidate array ordering; added tests for pandas/numpy/Decimal inputs. Release notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v0.9.3

acme_sre_jdoe: Installing 0.9.3 now and will run our integration tests. Quick question — what about TypeScript users who see lexicographic sorting? Any temporary server-side mitigation?

maria_ml: We can add a server-side defensive normalization in rerank handler to ensure `score` fields are cast to float before sending to clients. I'll open a small internal PR and cherry-pick to prod if needed. But prefer SDK fix first.

acme_sre_jdoe: Confirmed 0.9.3 resolves the issue for us. Scores are numeric and ordering is correct. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

sara_support: Closing loop — customer happy. Marking as resolved and adding a KB note: "Rerank: numeric scores serialized as strings due to SDK 0.9.2 Decimal handling — upgrade to 0.9.3".

jon_eng: Adding postmortem note: root cause was SDK serializer using fallback `str()` which converted Decimal/numpy types to strings. Impact limited to customers passing non-builtin numeric types into candidates. Action items: 1) add SDK validation, 2) server defensive cast, 3) add e2e test with pandas/numpy types.

sara_support: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
